newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish exports up 16.7 pct in Jan - exporters.
newsitem.headline: Turkish exports up 16.7 pct in Jan - exporters.

text.p: Turkish exports rose by 16.7 to $2.12 billion in January 1997 from $1.82 billion in the same period in 1996, the Turkish Exporters' Assembly (TIM) said in a statement on Thursday.

TIM chairman Okan Oguz said the increase was not so important because exports in January 1996 were adversely affected by Turkey's customs union agreement with the European Union which took effect from January 1, 1996.
"We will be able to see in March what direction developments are really taking," Oguz said.

Compared to January 1996, readywear exports rose by 25.6 percent to $654.6 million, metals exports jumped by 34.4 percent to $245.9 million and exports of textile and related raw materials grew by 16.4 percent to $227.3 million in January.
The biggest export growth was recorded in the electric-electronics sector with a rise of 35.8 percent to $156 million.
